rv.q: Everything you see, hear and feel is inherently theatrical — literality drops away like Dublin street noise as you head to an undiscovered country, and you start to feel things that the movie simply could not make you feel.
The show wins its standing ovations the old-fashioned way: with a love story, great songs, compelling characters and inventive stagecraft.
What's strange is the big-time boldness of its small-scale originality.

The most original and emotionally exhilarating of the trio is the new stage version of "Once," the offbeat 2007 movie musical about the unlikely Dublin romance of a depressed Irish street singer and a buoyantly unsinkable Czech immigrant.
Once is a small-scale but warmly affecting show, crafted with profound respect for the power of music.
And what was always wonderful about “Once,” its songs and its staging, has been magnified.
The result is a show that manages to be both intimate and theatrical, a rare combination that makes 'Once' one of the most satisfying musicals to reach Broadway in quite some time.
Once is a small-scale musical with a big heart, and it has been transferred to Broadway with unusual care and intelligence.
Broadway musicals spawned from movies are usually big, brash, bawdy affairs — think “Sister Act” and “Priscilla Queen of the Desert,” two giddy disco balls launched last season.
They make us forget, for hours at a stretch, that we're watching a show that's simply falling slowly in love with itself.
For “Once” the Broadway musical is in fact better than the movie.
This Broadway adaptation of the acclaimed 2007 indie film preserves the intimate, bittersweet spirit of the original while adding theatrical magic that feels organic rather than forced.
Happily, “Once” remains a rare combination of intelligence, warmth and musicality.
The wonderful musical “Once” is the sweetest and most romantic show on Broadway and proves that not all love stories lead to the bedroom.
Not a bad suggestion for the audience, either.

cn.t: Critics largely embrace this intimate Irish musical, praising its emotional depth and authenticity, though some find its melancholy songs repetitive. Most agree it's a rare, wise romantic show that casts a powerful spell.
